title: Nonzero circulations contain an arc-cycle
statement: Let $D$ be a digraph with finite vertex set $V$ and finite arc set $A$, and let $F$ be a field. If $f \colon A \to F$ is a circulation on $D$ — that is, $f$ lies in the cycle space $\mathcal{C}$ — and $f$ is not identically zero, then there exists an arc-cycle $c$ in $D$ (a nonempty closed arc-sequence) all of whose arcs lie in the support of $f$, i.e. every arc appearing in $c$ satisfies $f(a) \neq 0$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a circulation (lies in the cycle space)
replaced:
\emph{If \texttt{f} is a nonzero circulation, then \texttt{$\|$f$\|$} contains a
cycle.}
